title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-scratchpad-2026-03-04-ava
content:
Context:
- Canary rollout of release/2026-03-03 (image tag release-2026-03-03-9876) started at ~2026-03-03T22:10Z. Canary traffic: 5% to new revision. After ~3 hours, error rate on canary routes increased (5xxs, timeouts).
- Goal: capture breadcrumbs for what I tried, quick checks, and hypotheses before a formal postmortem.

Timeline & quick observations:
- 22:10Z: Deploy triggered via release pipeline (GitHub Actions -> ArgoCD sync).
- 22:45Z: Canary metrics quiet, no regression.
- 01:15Z: SLO alerts: canary latency p50/p95 increased; 502/504 spikes reported from Envoy LB.
- 01:22Z: Canary pods returning 502 with short response bodies; logs show upstream errors.
- 01:30Z: Rolled canary down to 0% traffic as temporary mitigation.

Commands I ran and outputs (copied verbatim where possible):
- kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=redwood-api -o wide
  -> canary pods (rev=release-9876) show CrashLoopBackOff for 2/3 pods, one Ready.

- kubectl logs -n prod deployment/redwood-api --selector=revision=release-9876 -c api
  -> stack traces: frequent timeouts when contacting redis-cluster: dial tcp 10.2.3.4:6379: i/o timeout
  -> repeated: "error fetching user-session: context deadline exceeded"

- kubectl describe pod <pod-id> -n prod
  -> Events show liveness probe failures and image pull ok. No OOMKilled.

- curl -v http://<canary-pod-ip>:8080/health
  -> 200 OK locally inside cluster; but when hitting service through envoy LB it 502s.

- curl to redis from within pod (kubectl exec -it pod -- redis-cli -h redis-cluster-host ping)
  -> sometimes PONG, sometimes connection timed out. Intermittent connectivity.

- Checked network policy changes around 2026-03-03T21:50Z (audit logs):
  -> No recent networkpolicy changes in prod. No k8s CNI upgrades recorded.

Artifact checks:
- Verified image digest used by ArgoCD vs artifact registry:
  - ArgoCD shows image: ghcr.io/redwood/api:release-2026-03-03-9876 -> digest sha256:aaaaaaaa
  - Registry shows build 9876 pushed with digest sha256:bbbbbbbb (mismatch!)
  - Hypothesis: image tag was reused and overwritten during parallel build/publish; ArgoCD pulled different digest than expected.

- S3 artifact (build tarball) checksum:
  -> local downloaded checksum matches CI artifact, but container registry digest mismatch remains suspicious.

Helm/rollout state & commands tried:
- argo rollouts get rollout redwood-api -n prod --watch
  -> rollout at 5% canary, progression paused by analysis due to error budget breach.

- kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-api -n prod --to-revision=42
  -> performed to rollback to last stable revision (rev 42). Observed: after undo, canary pods for rev 9876 terminated and stable pods scaled back up.

- Post-rollback: latency and error rates returned to baseline within ~12 minutes.

Error snippets seen in logs (raw):
- "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers
  service_name: \"redis-cluster\"
  connection failure: Dial tcp 10.2.3.4:6379: i/o timeout"
- "panic: unexpected nil pointer when reading session (userID=...)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Artifact tag reuse / image digest mismatch: CI pipeline pushed a new build with the same tag without immutably pinning digest; production Argo/registry mismatch caused a mix of code + infra assumptions leading to redis client incompatibility. Evidence: digest mismatch between ArgoCD view and registry.
2) Transient network flakiness to redis cluster (connectivity/iptables/CNI) exacerbated by new code path added in release (e.g., parallel session fetch) -> higher concurrency -> hitting a latent bug. Evidence: intermittent redis timeouts in canary pods.
3) Sidecar/proxy change introduced in release interacting poorly with Envoy config -> Envoy returning 502 while pod local health is OK. Evidence: local pod health endpoints OK but external LB 502.
4) Configuration drift: new release expected KV namespace key that wasn't present in prod causing code to hit an error path. Less evidence right now.

Immediate takeaways / checklist for next steps:
- Lockdown artifact immutability: ensure CI publishes immutable digests and Argo is configured to deploy by digest.
- Add sanity check step in pipeline: post-publish verify digest in registry matches the one referenced by the release manifest.
- Reproduce locally: pull digest sha256:bbbbbbbb and run in staging with synthetic canary traffic to try to reproduce redis timeouts.
- Check redis cluster monitoring (slow logs, connection counts) during the window 00:45-01:30Z.
- Search for any concurrent operators/jobs around 2026-03-03T21:30-22:30Z that might have affected network or redis config.
- Add more verbose redis client logs and connection metrics for next canary.

Notes for follow-up investigation (owners):
- Artifact ownership (Devon) -> verify pipeline publish semantics and why tag was overwritten.
- Infra/Networking (Imani) -> check CNI health, flannel/calico logs, any kube-proxy restarts.
- App owner (Samir) -> audit code change in release that touches session/redis code paths.

Quick reproduction commands I want to run next (in staging):
- docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/api@sha256:bbbbbbbb && docker run -e ENV=staging -it ghcr.io/redwood/api@sha256:bbbbbbbb /bin/sh -c 'npm start'
- run load test script that simulates session lookups: ./tools/loadtest --concurrency 200 --endpoint /api/session --duration 5m

Log snippets to capture (already pulled into logs bucket):
- s3://redwood-logs/prod/redwood-api/2026-03-03/canary/ -> saved stderr logs for canary pods.
- Sentinel alert snapshots in Grafana (panels: p95 latency, 5xx rate, envoy upstream failures).

Final short note (for PMs/incident page):
- Rolled canary back to stable due to increase in 5xxs/timeouts. Root cause TBD; primary lead: artifact immutability mismatch suspected. Next actions: artifact verification fixes + targeted staging repro.

-- Ava
